statement: For an absolutely continuous random variable X taking values in a sample space, a probability density function (PDF) f_X is a nonnegative function whose integral over any range of values gives the probability that X falls within that range: P(a <= X <= b) = \int_a^b f_X(x) dx, satisfying f_X(x) >= 0 everywhere and \int_{-\infty}^\infty f_X(x) dx = 1.

symbols.meaning: probability density function of random variable X evaluated at point x
a point in the sample space (possible value of X)
probability that X falls within the range [a, b]

properties.property: Nonnegativity: f_X(x) >= 0 for all points x in the sample space
properties.why: The integral represents a nonnegative area under the curve corresponding to probability

properties.property: Normalization: The total area under the entire density curve equals 1, i.e., \int_{-\infty}^\infty f_X(x) dx = 1
properties.why: The probability of the random variable falling within the set of all possible values is 100%

properties.property: Zero point probability: For any particular individual value x, P(X = x) = 0
properties.why: Probability density represents probability per unit length, giving zero area over a single point

properties.property: Relative likelihood: The ratio of PDF values f_X(x_1) / f_X(x_2) indicates how much more likely it is that the random variable is close to x_1 compared to x_2
properties.why: The PDF value provides the relative probability per unit length at any given point in a draw

properties.property: Monotonic scalar transformation: If Y = g(X) with differentiable monotonic g, then f_Y(y) = |(g^{-1})'(y)| * f_X(g^{-1}(y))
properties.why: Probability mass is conserved under change of variables scaled by the derivative of the inverse transformation

properties.property: Bijective vector transformation: If y = G(x) is bijective and differentiable on R^n, then p_Y(y) = f(G^{-1}(y)) * |det(dG^{-1}(z)/dz |_{z=y})|
properties.why: Volume scaling under multivariate change of variables is governed by the Jacobian determinant of the inverse map

properties.property: Convolution for independent sums: If U and V are independent random variables with densities, then f_{U+V}(x) = (f_U * f_V)(x) = \int_{-\infty}^\infty f_U(y) f_V(x - y) dy
properties.why: Obtained by bivariate change of variables Y = U + V, Z = V followed by marginalizing out Z

assumptions.assumption: The random variable is absolutely continuous
assumptions.breaks_when: The random variable is discrete or mixed, possessing point masses where individual points have non-zero probability.

assumptions.assumption: The density function is integrable and normalized over the sample space
assumptions.breaks_when: The total integral over the entire domain diverges or differs from 1 (improper or unnormalized distribution).

assumptions.assumption: Transformation mappings G are bijective and differentiable when applying standard change of variables
assumptions.breaks_when: The transformation is non-invertible, non-differentiable, or has a singular Jacobian matrix.

failure_modes.signature: Treating f_X(x) as P(X = x), leading to contradictions when f_X(x) > 1 or expecting point values to sum to 1
failure_modes.cause: Confusing probability density (probability per unit length) with discrete probability mass; for continuous variables, P(X = x) = 0.

failure_modes.mode: Omission of multiple preimages under non-monotonic transformations
failure_modes.signature: Underestimating the density of transformed variable Y = g(X)
failure_modes.cause: Using single-branch inverse formula when g(x) = y has multiple roots, failing to sum over all solutions g_k^{-1}(y).

failure_modes.mode: Omission of Jacobian determinant in multivariate transformations
failure_modes.signature: Incorrect transformed density that does not integrate to 1
failure_modes.cause: Failing to account for local volume distortion by omitting |det(dG^{-1}(z)/dz)|.
